note: TUBA4A-associated spastic ataxia (SPAX11) presents primarily with gait disturbances and early oculomotor signs, making a late onset of cerebellar dysarthria plausible.

evidence.text: In two families with SPAX11 due to the TUBA4A p.Glu415Lys variant, gait disturbance was a constant sign at onset, while other signs correlated with varying disease durations up to 11 and 33 years.

source.title: A new genetic cause of spastic ataxia: the p.Glu415Lys variant in TUBA4A
source.quote: Gait disturbance was a constant sign at the onset. Nystagmus… with a short disease duration. Dentate nuclei hyperintensities … two patients from F1 with disease duration of 11 and 33 years…

evidence.text: Screening revealed 12 patients with TUBA4A variants presenting with spasticity and/or cerebellar ataxia with variable age of onset, expanding the clinical spectrum.

source.title: De novo and inherited monoallelic variants in TUBA4A cause ataxia and spasticity
source.quote: Taken together, we report 12 patients presenting with spasticity and/or cerebellar ataxia and harbouring a predicted pathogenic TUBA4A missense mutation

numbers.metric: reported affected patients with spasticity and/or cerebellar ataxia
